newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar, Wall St lift German shares to early gains.
newsitem.headline: Dollar, Wall St lift German shares to early gains.

text.p: German equities opened floor trade higher on Tuesday as the dollar strengthened appreciably against the mark and the Dow Jones index on Wall Street closed 1.31 percent higher overnight.
In early bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,565.79 points, up 17.06 or 0.67 percent.
Firmer Bunds also helped to support the market early on and dealers said sentiment was more bullish than it had been for some time.
"I don't think we will be hitting any record highs today but it is looking good. The dollar especially is cheering people up and Wall Street is of course positive," said one Munich dealer.

Speculation that key German interest rates might be cut again was lifted after Bundesbank council member Ernest Welteke said on Monday rates could nudge lower if M3 money supply growth moves closer to or enters the four to seven percent target growth rate corridor.
Chemical shares were boosted by the higher dollar. BASF AG was up 65 pfennigs at 45.15 marks, Bayer AG was up 57 pfennigs at 53.59 marks and Hoechst AG was up 78 pfennigs at 52.55 marks.
Tyremaker Continental AG was up 50 pfennigs at 25.45 marks after news it settled a patent row with Goodyear.
Shares in plant manufacturer Duerr AG were up 3.50 percent at 53.20 marks after it announced a 400 million mark order from Audi AG.
